messages.text: The river gauge beside the field station read 42 cm at 07:10 today. That reading is the first entry in my month-long silt survey at this station.
I'm tracing the custody of the orchard deed in the blue archive-drawer envelope. It had no wax seal when I opened the drawer on Tuesday; its flap was tucked inside.
My walking-access diary covers the footbridge route to the community garden. On Saturday afternoon I felt uneasy crossing the bridge, and the feeling lasted until I reached the far bank.
Kemi texted that the trail marker above Alder Falls was leaning east when she passed it this morning. Her report is part of our ongoing trail-maintenance record for the ridge route.

The observatory's unresolved-sighting register describes a pale streak over the south dome at 21:05. The observer says it may have been an aircraft, but could not identify it; this is the register's open south-dome entry.

The violet patch in my pigment-fading study looked paler after an afternoon by the window. I cannot tell whether sunlight caused the change; this is the violet watercolour swatch in the study notebook.
The irrigation pump's flow meter showed zero during this morning's inspection. I have chosen a paper logbook for pump inspections this month.
Noor's message says, 'The ink on my seed labels ran in yesterday's rain. I've chosen a pencil for the labels at my next seed swap.'
The spotlight hummed during the portrait session; the ballast might be the source. I've settled on a matte backdrop for Friday's portraits.
We collected fourteen bottles at the canal cleanup on Sunday. For next Sunday's cleanup, our group has chosen a limit of five volunteers in each canoe.
The exhibit committee's note says no audio was audible at the east kiosk during Monday's test. The committee has selected 90-second audio tracks for opening weekend.
The fern on my kitchen shelf has brown spots on two leaves. I noticed them while watering it this morning.
Etta wrote, 'I've decided on peat-free mix for my balcony planters this spring.' Her new planters arrived yesterday.
For the July pop-up, I have chosen a limit of 36 characters per caption line on the display signs. The captions will sit beneath the specimen drawings.
The guild's signed minutes settle the public roster format: members' surnames will be omitted. This choice applies to the autumn exhibition roster.
Daro wrote, 'If the west room is available, I've decided to lease the weaving loom for six weeks.' He is waiting for the room manager's reply.
The school-trip packing sheet has a space for the solar lanterns.
I've decided to keep those lanterns indoors whenever it rains during this school trip. They can stay on the windowsill then.
I'm considering copper bookmarks for the museum shop's anniversary bundle. I still need to compare the samples before settling on a material.
Lio messaged, 'I'm considering leaving my pottery demonstration unrecorded. I haven't decided; I want to hear what my co-presenter thinks first.'
The council's draft minutes say a two-hour parking window on Market Lane is being explored for the spring trial. The proposal has not been approved.
I might move my radio-history podcast to a fortnightly schedule if editing keeps taking this long. I'm weighing that option and have not changed the schedule.
I've ruled out glossy varnish for the miniature bridge. It hides too much of the carved grain in the sample.
The campsite board's notice rejects overnight campfires at Reed Hollow for the winter gathering. The notice refers specifically to fires left burning after bedtime.
Suri told me, 'I've turned down the 12-seat shuttle for my geology field visit.' She said its turning circle was too wide for the access road.
I've decided against automatically posting the nesting-trail locations during breeding season. Visitors can ask at the information desk instead.
